title: Put the keys in the drawer standing open, do another job, then fetch them back opening only that drawer
instruction: Put the keys in the drawer of the chest that is standing open and push it shut, holding the chest by a carry handle with one hand while the other works the drawer. Then put the glasses case in the leather tray and take both arms back to where they started. Then take the keys back out, opening only the drawer you put them in (once the keys are put away, never open any other drawer), put them in the key dish, push that drawer shut and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Putting something away and finding it again later is an everyday need: a home robot that forgets which drawer it used has to open every drawer or gives up. Once the drawer is shut the four look the same, so only memory says where the keys are.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A polished white marble top 6 mm thick, from 13 to 47 cm forward and 25 cm to each side, fixed. (2) On it, a low walnut-stained beech chest of four identical drawers side by side (0.6 kg, standing on furniture glides), 46 cm wide, 14.2 cm deep and 7.8 cm tall, its drawer fronts 29 cm forward, its middle on the centre line, with a brass carry handle on top near each end (bars 8 cm long and 1.2 cm thick running front to back, 14 cm either side of the centre line, 10 cm above the marble). (3) Its four drawers (0.2 kg each): fronts 10.1 x 5.8 cm with a brass knob 2.5 cm across sticking out 3.8 cm, felt-lined boxes 9.6 cm wide, 11.8 cm deep and 4.2 cm tall; they run stiffly (about 1.8 N to move one, felt runners with a magnetic catch that pulls a drawer the last 12 mm shut) and pull out at most 12.5 cm. One drawer stands about 3 cm open at the start: number (seed mod 4) counted from the left starting at 0 (with the default seed, drawer 2, the third from the left). (4) A bunch of keys (45 g) lying flat on the table 21.5 cm forward and 29 cm right of the centre line, pointing forward: a black ABS car key fob 2.9 x 2.2 x 1.5 cm with three buttons, a steel split ring 1.6 cm across and a brass house key 3 cm long, 7.2 cm long in all. (5) A navy hard-shell glasses case (70 g), 15.5 x 5.8 x 3.6 cm, lying 22 cm forward and 29.5 cm left of the centre line along the forward direction. (6) A tan leather valet tray, 20 x 9 cm with 1.8 cm walls, its middle 40 cm forward and 30 cm left of the centre line, fixed. (7) A white glazed ceramic key dish 9.6 cm across and 2.2 cm deep with a blue rim, its middle 40 cm forward and 30 cm right of the centre line, fixed. The layout is the same in every trial except which drawer stands open, as in the screenshot.
scoring: A drawer counts as shut within 4 mm of shut and as opened past 8 mm. The keys are put away when the fob is inside the drawer that stood open and all four drawers are shut. 0.0 if, once the keys have been put away, any other drawer is opened (latched). Otherwise 1.0: the keys put away; then, with them still put away, the glasses case put into the tray (lying in it, under 25 degrees from flat) and both arms back where they started at the same time; and at the end the keys in the key dish, the glasses case in the tray, all four drawers shut and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75: the keys put away, the glasses case and the arms as above at some point, and the keys in the key dish at the end; 0.5: the keys put away and, while they were, the glasses case put in the tray and both arms back where they started, at some point; 0.25: the keys put away at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the chest, its drawers, the keys and the glasses case still.
reset_notes: Put the keys, the glasses case and the chest back in place and push every drawer shut; the open drawer is set again from the seed at every reset.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: a drawer's stiff runners are a drive that holds it where it is with up to 1.8 N, and the magnetic catch a spring that pulls it the last 12 mm shut. The chest's glides on the polished marble have a friction of 0.045 (it slides at about 0.6 N), so a drawer pulled or pushed with nothing holding the chest drags the whole chest. The keys are one rigid body. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
